scheme_name: Relief During Natural Calamities Such as Cyclone, Flood or Fire (Sainik Welfare)
description:
The Relief During Natural Calamities Scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to provide assistance to individuals and families affected by natural disasters such as cyclones, floods, and fires.

This scheme is particularly focused on the welfare of ex-servicemen and their dependents who face hardships due to such calamities.

The scheme was officially launched in the year 2006 under the Ministry of Defence.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide immediate financial assistance to ex-servicemen and their families in the aftermath of natural disasters.

The scheme aims to ensure that the affected individuals receive timely support to help them recover from the impacts of these disasters.

The government has set measurable targets to provide relief to a minimum of 10,000 families annually who are affected by natural calamities.

The financial assistance provided under this scheme varies based on the severity of the calamity and the extent of damage incurred by the beneficiaries.

For instance, in the case of a cyclone or flood, the assistance may range from INR 5,000 to INR 20,000 per family.

In the event of a fire disaster, the financial aid may be up to INR 15,000 per family.

The scheme also includes provisions for the distribution of essential items such as food, clothing, and temporary shelter to the affected individuals.

Eligibility for this scheme is primarily focused on ex-servicemen and their dependents.

To qualify for assistance, the applicant must be a registered ex-serviceman with the respective Zila Sainik Board.

There are no specific age limits imposed for eligibility under this scheme.

However, the income criteria state that the annual income of the applicant should not exceed INR 3 lakh.

The applicant must also provide proof of residence in the affected area to ensure that the assistance reaches those who are genuinely in need.

The application process for this scheme is straightforward and designed to facilitate quick relief.

Interested beneficiaries must fill out the application form available at the local Zila Sainik Board office or on the official website of the Ministry of Defence.

The required documents include a copy of the ex-serviceman's discharge certificate, proof of residence, and any documentation that verifies the extent of damage caused by the calamity.

Once the application is submitted, the Zila Sainik Board will conduct an assessment of the damage.

This assessment is crucial for determining the amount of financial assistance to be provided.

The timeline for disbursement of funds is typically within 15 days of the application being approved.

This quick turnaround is essential to ensure that the beneficiaries receive the support they need in a timely manner.

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Defence, specifically the Directorate of Sainik Welfare.

Each state has its own Zila Sainik Board that oversees the implementation of the scheme at the local level.

Contact details for the Directorate of Sainik Welfare can be found on the official Ministry of Defence website.

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also emphasizes the importance of rehabilitation and resettlement of affected families.

The government collaborates with various NGOs and local organizations to provide additional support and resources to the affected individuals.

Statistical data indicates that over 50,000 families have benefited from this scheme since its inception in 2006.

The scheme has been instrumental in providing relief during major disasters such as the 2013 Uttarakhand floods and the 2019 Kerala floods.

In 2019 alone, approximately INR 2 crore was disbursed to ex-servicemen and their families affected by the Kerala floods.

The scheme also includes provisions for psychological support and counseling for those who have experienced trauma due to natural disasters.

This aspect of the scheme is particularly important as it addresses the mental health needs of the affected individuals.

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to educate ex-servicemen about the availability of this scheme and how to access it.

These campaigns are conducted through various media channels including print, television, and social media platforms.

The Relief During Natural Calamities Scheme is part of a broader framework of disaster management policies in India.

The government has established a National Disaster Management Authority to coordinate relief efforts across various states.

This authority works in conjunction with the Ministry of Defence to ensure that ex-servicemen receive the necessary support during times of crisis.

In conclusion, the Relief During Natural Calamities Scheme is a vital initiative aimed at providing timely assistance to ex-servicemen and their families affected by natural disasters.

With specific financial assistance amounts and a streamlined application process, the scheme ensures that those who have served the nation are not left to fend for themselves in times of need.

The ongoing efforts to improve the scheme and increase awareness among potential beneficiaries demonstrate the government's commitment to the welfare of ex-servicemen.

The scheme continues to evolve to meet the changing needs of the population it serves, ensuring that no ex-serviceman is left behind during natural calamities.
